name: Devil, Alecto
body:
Alecto (Lesser Fury)
CR 4

Disheveled hair, mottled white-and-brown wings with rotted feathers, and wild eyes, this woman could be a fallen angel or a risen fiend. Her whip cracks while she eagerly looks around for prey.

XP 1,200
LN Medium outsider (devil, extraplanar, lawful)
Init +4; Senses darkvision 60 ft., see in darkness, true seeing; Perception +11

DEFENSE

AC 17, touch 15, flat-footed 12 (+4 Dex, +1 dodge, +2 natural)
hp 37 (5d10+10)
Fort +6, Ref +7, Will +4
DR 5/good; Immune fire, poison; Resist acid 10, cold 10

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., fly 50 ft. (good)
Melee whip +9 (1d3+3 plus entangle) or 2 claws +8 (1d4+3)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 8th; concentration +11)

Constant—true seeing
At will—cause fear (DC 15), greater teleport (self plus 50 lbs. of objects only)
1/day—terrible remorse (DC 18), summon (level 3, 1 alecto or 1d4 lemures, 50%)

STATISTICS

Str 16, Dex 19, Con 15, Int 14, Wis 17, Cha 18
Base Atk +5; CMB +8; CMD 22
Feats Combat Reflexes, DodgeB, Weapon Focus (whip), Whip Mastery
Skills Acrobatics +12, Fly +18, Intimidate +12, Knowledge (planes, religion) +10, Perception +11, Sense Motive +11, Stealth +12
Languages Celestial, Draconic, Infernal; telepathy 100 ft.
SQ implacable

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Entangle (Su)

On a successful hit, an alecto can order her whip to entangle opponents of any size as an animate rope spell (CL 12th, DC 16). This ability only works for a whip that the alecto is wielding. The save DC is Dexterity-based.

Implacable (Su)

As a standard action, an alecto can designate a creature as her quarry, thus becoming able of locating it as if the creature was marked with a brand of tracking. An alecto receives a +2 insight bonus on attack rolls made against her quarry, and all critical threats are automatically confirmed; in addition, the quarry suffers a -2 penalty on saving throws against the alecto’s supernatural and spell-like abilities. An alecto can have no more than one quarry at a time but can change her designated quarry whenever she wills as a standard action.

ECOLOGY

Environment any (Hell)
Organization solitary
Treasure standard

These fierce-looking winged women with snakes for hair exist for vengeance and retribution, particularly for crimes of children against their parents. Also known as “the Kindly Ones,” alectos are the rare devils who are not truly evil.

Nonetheless, they are avenging spirits of justice and beat their prey with scourges (whips that deal normal damage and can harm creatures with natural armor) and snakes, driving them to madness and despair until the ritual of purification cleansed them of their sins. They are hardly limited to punishing patricide and matricide, of course, and may be unleashed for punishment of any horrible crime the gods demand, but they are not inherently cruel. They are simply remorseless in their pursuit of harsh and painful justice.

These immortal embodiments of vengeance are reborn whenever slain by mortals, rising to life again in the outer planes to be sent forth again.

Knowing this deathless cycle awaits them, alectos are dauntless and gleefully wade into combat with their weapons, focusing on those whose misdeeds have drawn their ire. If attacked by something other than their prey, an alecto is likely to lash at it once or twice as a deterrent so they can deal with their prey, but turn on attackers who persist, as all children are guilty of some crime against their parents (no matter how small or petty) and thus deserve punishment if prompted.
